# CFF test fonts

Small OpenType CFF fonts for the host tests of the TrueType/CFF engine (`lib/EpdFont/ttf/`). The CFF rasterizer
is checked byte-for-byte against FreeType's CFF driver, which the host oracle (`test/ttf_rasterizer`) compiles in.
Every file here is generated by `lib/EpdFont/scripts/make_cff_fixtures.py`; do not edit them by hand.

| Font | What it is | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NotoSansJP-Cff.otf`, `NotoSerifJP-Cff.otf` | CID-keyed subsets of Noto Sans / Serif CJK JP Regular, subroutines kept | the CID-keyed path: FDSelect, per-FD Private dicts, local and global subroutines |
| `NotoSansJP-CffFlat.otf`, `NotoSerifJP-CffFlat.otf` | the same subsets with every subroutine inlined (`desubroutinize()`) | outlines without subroutine calls, to tell a subroutine fault from an operator fault |
| `NotoSansJP-CffSlanted.otf` | `NotoSansJP-CffFlat` with the top DICT FontMatrix `[0.001 0 0.0002 0.001 0 0]` | a non-identity FontMatrix |
| `NotoSansJP-TrueType.ttf` | `NotoSansJP-CffFlat` as TrueType: each cubic turned into quadratics within one font unit (fontTools' `Cu2QuPen`) | the device bench's run of the same characters as CFF and as TrueType (`bench/ttf_raster_main.cpp`) |
| `CffOperators.otf` | a name-keyed font, one glyph per Type 2 operator family | every operator, hintmask/cntrmask with 8 and 9 stems, seac, subroutines nested 15 deep |
| `NotoSansDevanagari-Shaping-Regular.ttf`, `-Bold.ttf` | TrueType subsets of Noto Sans Devanagari holding the code points of 16 Devanagari words (conjuncts, reph, matras, nukta, ZWJ, Marathi and Nepali forms) plus U+0020, U+200C, U+200D and U+25CC; unhinted, GDEF, GSUB and GPOS kept whole, each under 64 KB | step 2 PR 2's shaping tests: `OtShaperReference.TheTrueTypeSubsetShapesAsHarfBuzz` checks `lib/OtShaper` against HarfBuzz's runs for them (`test/ttf_font/ExpectedGlyphRuns.h`) |
| `NotoSansDevanagari-Book-Regular.ttf`, `NotoSansBengali-Book-Regular.ttf`, `NotoSansTamil-Book-Regular.ttf`, `NotoSansMalayalam-Book-Regular.ttf` | TrueType subsets of the unhinted Noto Sans Regular of each script, holding the code points of its book's XHTML (`test/epubs/test_shaped_<script>.epub`) plus U+0020, U+200C, U+200D and U+25CC; GDEF, GSUB and GPOS kept whole, each under 128 KB | the shaped-Indic books: each is laid out with its font as the shaping face of every font and style, for its `EpubPipelineTest` golden and `ShapingRulesTest`'s rules |

The Noto subsets hold ASCII U+0020-007E, the marks `、。「」・ー`, hiragana U+3041-3093, katakana U+30A1-30F3 and the
kanji `日本語文字書読鬱慶議驚龍鑑響漢点線曲円角` (288 glyphs each). They are subset without hinting, with the `kern`
layout feature only. `TtfEmboldenTest` reads the dense kanji 鬱書慶議驚 of `NotoSansJP-TrueType.ttf`,
`NotoSansJP-Cff.otf` and `NotoSerifJP-Cff.otf` (synthetic bold's counters, spec 7.2).

`CffOperators.otf` ("CFF Operators Test") is this repository's own test data, written by the script with fontTools'
`FontBuilder`; it contains no third-party data. It has no glyph using `random` (FreeType's result for it is not
reproducible). Its bounding boxes are fixed values, since fontTools cannot trace the arithmetic operators.

## Regenerating

Download the two sources into one directory, then, from the repository root:

    python lib/EpdFont/scripts/make_cff_fixtures.py --source-dir <dir with the two OTFs> --out test/fixtures/fonts

The script checks both sha256 values (it does not download) and writes only the seven fonts. The output is
byte-identical on every run; `git status --short test/fixtures` shows no change after a second run. Needs
`fonttools`.

The Devanagari subsets and their expected HarfBuzz runs come from `lib/EpdFont/scripts/make_shaping_fixtures.py`.
Download the two Noto Sans Devanagari TTFs into one directory, then, from the repository root:

    python lib/EpdFont/scripts/make_shaping_fixtures.py --source-dir <dir with the two TTFs> --fonts-out test/fixtures/fonts --header-out test/ttf_font/ExpectedGlyphRuns.h

It checks both sha256 values (it does not download), writes the two subsets and the header, and is byte-identical on
every run. Needs `fonttools` and `uharfbuzz`. The words, the conversion and `round_px` are crosspoint-reader PR #3787's
`generate_fixtures.py` (SSafayet / @SSafayet).

The shaped-book subsets come from `lib/EpdFont/scripts/make_shaped_book_fonts.py`, from the books, so regenerate the
books first when their text changes (`python -I test/epubs/make_test_shaped_indic.py`). Download the four Noto Sans
Regular TTFs (Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil, Malayalam) into one directory, then, from the repository root:

    python lib/EpdFont/scripts/make_shaped_book_fonts.py --source-dir <dir with the four TTFs> --books test/epubs --fonts-out test/fixtures/fonts

It checks the four sha256 values (it does not download), fails a font of 131,072 bytes or more, writes only the four
fonts, and is byte-identical on every run. Needs `fonttools`.
